Hi Mel — saw you tagged me. I haven’t seen your leg, so can’t diagnose over the internet, but your story sounds like a classic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy from the jump in volume rather than a tear: morning stiffness, sore to squeeze a few cm above the heel, eases with running then aches later, and a bit of thickening. The lack of a pop is reassuring.

Afew things. Don’t stretch it hard till it burns — that often flares it up, especially first thing. And I’d skip the cortisone shot near the tendon if you can; it can settle symptoms for a week or two but weakens the tendon and carries a rupture risk. Heel drops off a step are okay, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence now — do them with the knee straight and bent, slow up and down, load it so it’s challenging but not awful. On bad days, isometric calf holds (30–45 sec) can help settle it.

Use pain as your guide: up to 3/10 while loading is generally okay if it’s back to baseline by next morning. If it’s worse the next day or you’re limping around the office, that session was too much — back off the volume and impact for a few days. Don’t run through increasing morning stiffness.

Most important: if you get a sudden pop, feel like you’ve been kicked in the back of the leg, or can’t push off, stop running and the calf work and get it checked urgently that day — GP or ED — because that could be a rupture.

One general note: some antibiotics, especially quinolones, are linked with tendon problems. If you’ve been on any recently, mention it when you get assessed.

If it’s not clearly settling in 3–4 weeks, or it’s getting worse despite backing off, see a sports physio. You’re in Bayswater, so any decent local sports physio is fine — doesn’t need to be me. Good luck with Rottnest.
